Hi,
I am Prashant , from BITS Pilani , India , currently in my 3rd year of study of Engineering .I know following languages and have prior experience of working in them 
C/C++,Java,Python 
PHP,HTML,CSS,
Javascript,MySQL,
jQuery,Flotr.js,Angular.js

As a participant in GSOC 2014 I am interested in working on Interactive Visualization using rCharts.Although I dont have any prior experience of working with R or rCharts but after going through the above links a lot became clear about rCharts.From what I have understood the project is about creating a single unified interface using Javascript libraries.
while going through the rCharts following ideas popped up in my mind which can be corporated in the project(first draft we need to discuss these in details):
  • Addition of functionalities like Panning , Selective Zooming , Curve Tracing using flotr.js library
  • Exporting the rCharts as PDF.(A button to download them as pdf)
  • Incorporating more Javascript libraries like flotr.js which have specialized graphs
As of now as I dont have any prior experience of working in R or rCharts I would like to know what are the required levels of proficiency in them and what are the prerequisites for this project.
Hope my insights are useful.

with regards,
Prashant Kiran

messages.subject: Re: Interactive Visualizations with rCharts
parts:
Hi Prashant,

Your observations on rCharts are quite right, in that it is more of a meta-framework that provides a unified interface to multiple javascript visualization libraries.

Given your background, it would be useful for you to familiarize yourself with R. Here is an excellent Coursera course that should get you up to speed pretty quickly, especially if you are already proficient with programming, which certainly seems to be the case

https://www.coursera.org/course/compdata

I will be updating the project description and test criteria this weekend. As indicated, I am open to suggestions, since we will be charting rather new territories.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: Interactive Visualizations with rCharts
parts:
Hi Shubham,

Glad to know of your interest in interactive data visualizations. I will be updating the project page for rCharts shortly, with details on the proposed project and skill set requirements.

On Python support, while I think it is interesting, it would be outside the scope of G-Soc-R, since our priority here is to build tools for R users. However, there are some design decisions that can make it easy to create a Python port. I would be happy to discuss this further as well.

Stay tuned for the project description, and we will take it from there.

Best,
Ramnath
